name: Arm Triangle from Hindulotine
description: Arm Triangle from Hindulotine requires a new head-and-arm enclosure. Free the raised leg and establish the trapped shoulder before considering the choke.
summary: The Arm Triangle encloses the head and one arm so the attacker's upper arm and the defender's trapped shoulder compress opposite sides of the neck.
overview:
The attacker has an arm around the head and the opponent's arm across the neck, commonly after establishing a top pin. Hindu Control supplies a leg-in guillotine enclosure. An Arm Triangle requires a newly positioned head-and-arm loop; the high rubber-guard leg is not its defining choking surface.

Establish a stable pin or equivalent control with one opposing arm across the neck. Place the attacking upper arm beside one side of the neck without levering the head backward. Prevent the trapped arm from returning between the bodies while keeping the elbow comfortable. Close the arm loop without changing the neck into a twisting position.

Use positional closure rather than a neck crank, practice the control without pressure, and release the shoulder and neck at any tap.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting — head-and-arm choke / kata gatame](https://www.grapplearts.com/how-to-do-the-head-and-arm-choke-aka-kata-gatame/); [Ben Eddy — Hindu Control to Hindulotine](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y5ZQNgG2hNc).

flashcards.question: Arm Triangle after Hindu Control: which direction should the opponent's trapped arm cross?
flashcards.answer: Across the front of their neck. Establish a stable pin or equivalent control with one opposing arm crossing toward the other side. Their shoulder and your upper arm must then enclose the neck without twisting it.
flashcards.answer_line: Across the front of their neck

flashcards.answer: On the opposite side of the neck. The attacking upper arm and the opponent's own shoulder form the two sides of the enclosure. Preserve head alignment when placing the arm.
flashcards.answer_line: On the opposite side of the neck

plausible: Alongside the captured shoulder
Below chest, clear of the neck
trap: Across jaw, turning the head away

flashcards.question: Arm Triangle practice: which head movement must be avoided as the enclosure closes?
flashcards.answer: Twisting the head away from its spinal alignment. Remove space by positioning the enclosing arm and shoulder, not by cranking the neck. Keep the practice unloaded until the geometry and release are clear.

plausible: Head following an aligned body turn

trap: Head moving with the shoulder line

flashcards.answer: The opponent's own shoulder beside their neck. The attacking upper arm closes one side of the neck while the opponent's own shoulder closes the other. Establish this separate arm-and-shoulder arrangement after releasing the original leg-in enclosure.

plausible: Your shin replacing the arm loop

defender.description: Arm Triangle from Hindulotine (defender): Recover the arm before it crosses the neck and becomes enclosed. Maintain an early frame between the shoulder and head while the loop is still open.
defender.overview:
The attacker has an arm around the head and the opponent's arm across the neck, commonly after establishing a top pin. Hindu Control supplies a leg-in guillotine enclosure. An Arm Triangle requires a newly positioned head-and-arm loop; the high rubber-guard leg is not its defining choking surface.

Recover the arm before it crosses the neck and becomes enclosed. Maintain an early frame between the shoulder and head while the loop is still open. An upper arm beside the neck plus your own shoulder on the other side is the key threat.

Move the hips and shoulders together while space remains; do not turn the head alone. Stop before dizziness or impaired awareness instead of treating top position as a prerequisite for danger. Rebuild a safe arm position once the head-and-arm loop is open.

Use positional closure rather than a neck crank, practice the control without pressure, and release the shoulder and neck at any tap.

Protect the neck by keeping an early frame between the trapped shoulder and the closing arm. If that enclosure opens and the attacker remains on top, continue the escape with supported hip movement and a short shrimp to return a knee inside; do not bridge against a secured neck.
